subject.title: tools.deny not enforced for claude-cli backend MCP — agents can call denied MCP tools

question: Which enforcement boundary should own `tools.deny` for Claude CLI MCP servers: OpenClaw's generated MCP config, Claude's native `--disallowedTools`, or a fail-closed unsupported-policy path?
rationale: All options affect a security boundary and can either overexpose MCP tools or break existing Claude CLI MCP workflows, so automation should not choose the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Filter before Claude handoff
options.body: Apply the effective per-agent MCP deny policy while generating the strict Claude MCP config, and only use server-level removal for entries that safely map to whole-server authorization.

options.title: Map denies to Claude arguments
options.body: Translate matching deny entries into Claude `--disallowedTools` while keeping the generated config intact, if maintainers accept Claude as the enforcing boundary.

options.title: Fail closed for unenforceable policy
options.body: Refuse to launch Claude CLI sessions when configured MCP deny entries cannot be represented safely, with clear diagnostics and docs.

recommendation.title: Filter before Claude handoff
recommendation.body: Apply the effective per-agent MCP deny policy while generating the strict Claude MCP config, and only use server-level removal for entries that safely map to whole-server authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across shared bundle-MCP config, CLI adapter, and recent CLI MCP boundary work.
